title: Left, Root, Right

concept.title: Three ways to visit all nodes
body: A **traversal** visits every node of the tree exactly once, in some order. The three classical depth-first orders differ only in **when the root is visited**, compared with its two subtrees:

For a **binary search tree** (a tree where the left subtree has smaller values than the root and the right subtree has larger values) the in-order walk lists the values in increasing order. The list `out` is passed down so that all calls add to the same list.

statement: Print the values of a binary tree in in-order: first the left subtree, then the root, then the right subtree (the same rule inside every subtree). Print all values on one line separated by spaces.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: The values in in-order on one line.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The left subtree is 9, then the root 3, then the right subtree: 15 20 7.

hints: Visit the left subtree first, then add the root value, then visit the right subtree.
Pass a list to the recursive function and append to it.

input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def inorder(root, out):
    if root is None:
        return
    inorder(root.left, out)
    out.append(root.val)
    inorder(root.right, out)
